guard: `cotal run` refuses an unroutable verb before any plane opens, printing the usage line, and that usage line names every verb the gate routes
proveWith: pnpm mutation-proof --config implementations/runtime/smoke/mutations/run-command-usage.json   # --config resolves against the repo root, never the cwd
why: This suite is the runtime package's `test` script, which the Windows required job runs with no
broker on the box, so it grades the one part of `cotal run` that must never touch the wire: the
verb gate. Two obligations, one mutant each: the gate itself (U1), and the agreement between
the gate's verb list and the usage text it prints, two hand-kept lists (U2). U1 shows why the
usage cell and not the exit-code cell is the discriminator: with the gate gone the dispatcher
opens the planes against an unreachable server and the connect helper exits 1 on its own, so
the exit code still reads 1 and only the missing usage line tells the two refusals apart.

mutations.name: the verb gate is gone, so an unroutable verb reaches the planes
mutations.expectRed: and the usage line on stderr
mutations.cell: and the usage line on stderr
mutations.note: Measured 2026-09-03: seven reds, the usage-line cells of both refusals and every verb-naming cell (the usage string was never printed), while both exit-code cells stay green because the connect helper exits 1 against the unreachable server; 3 ok, 7 failed.

mutations.name: the usage line loses a verb the gate still routes
mutations.note: The two lists drift independently; this is the drift the loop of verb cells exists to catch. Measured 2026-09-03: exactly one red, the `ps` cell, 9 ok, 1 failed. Re-anchored 2026-09-06 when `ps` grew `[--endpoint <ep>]` in the usage line.
